card.band: 8h. The patch-from lever is large and distinct, which gives dense credit. A frontier agent finds a part of the match-finder gain but not all. A weaker model gets only compiler-level tweaks.
card.cheat: Lowering the level or the ratio is caught by the size gate. Hidden inputs differ from the visible ones.
card.grading: Gate: round-trip exact, output decodable by the stock decoder, compressed size not exceeding the baseline by more than 1%. Score is by median wall-time speedup on hidden tar pairs (patch-from) and small-block sets. Reward is 2^u - 1, with S taken from the reference.
card.reference: zstd v1.5.7 measured at 4.9x for --patch-from lvl18 (210s to 42.7s) and 280 to 310 MB/s at 4KB blocks.
card.task: /app ships zstd v1.5.6 as a history-less snapshot. The agent speeds up --patch-from at high levels (18-21) and level-1 small-block compression and dictionary compression, as the 1.5.7 PRs did, and keeps the format and API valid.

source_notes: Levers: PRs #4144 #4165 (small-data compression), #4170 (dictionary ~+5%), #4276 (faster --patch-from high levels), #4288 (ratio), #4136/#4176/#4178 (block boundaries). Headline claim "up to +30%" not backed by the table (max +20%). --patch-from 3-5x is the large, distinct lever. Equivalence: compressed bytes change by design (ratio PRs), so gate on round-trip + size not exceeding baseline.
source_version: zstd v1.5.6 (page title compares 1.5.6 vs 1.5.7) -> zstd v1.5.7

facts.claim: zstd v1.5.7 release exists (tag page; released 19 Feb, 2025 per search results)
Licence is BSD (Meta copyright, 'BSD License for Zstandard software'); the three BSD conditions match BSD-3-Clause
--patch-from level 18: 210 s to 42.7 s (x4.9), linux-6.13 vs 6.12, 6 threads; level 19 x4.4, 20 x3.8, 21 x3.1
Small-block level 1 on Silesia, 4 KB: 280 to 310 MB/s (+10%); 32 KB is the largest gain at +20%
Release notes headline 'up to +30%' small-data wording exists, but the table's maximum is +20%
--patch-from size at level 18 changed 5,584,219 to 5,075,507 bytes (about 10% smaller), so the size gate has headroom in the reference's favour

PR #4276 'fix speed of --patch-from mode at high compression levels' merged into dev on Feb 6 2025 and touches lib/compress/zstdmt_compress.c and zstd_compress_internal.h; it skips an internal CDict duplicating reference content and removes the wait on first-job dictionary loading
PR #4276 benchmark on i7-9700K, 6 threads: level 18 208 s to 34 s (about 6.1x); the release table's 4.9x is a different pair and machine
ProgramBench zstd task exists in a public benchmark

full_card.band: 8h. Frontier agent likely recovers part of the patch-from gain (PR text names the approach), with partial credit per level and per block size. Full 4.9x is hard. Weaker model gets compiler-level tweaks only.
full_card.build_cost: about 3-4 days: grader needs hidden tar pair corpus (linux 6.12/6.13 or sized-down substitute), small-block sets, timing harness, and a test runner. Smoke build is green, but its test step parsed 0 tests (tests_total 0), so the suite is not wired up and the grader must be written by hand.
full_card.deliverable: Patched zstd library/CLI in /app that speeds up --patch-from at levels 18-21 and level-1 small-block and dictionary compression, keeps format and API valid.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Size gate blocks lowering level or ratio (lvl15 patch output is about 14% larger than lvl18). Stock decoder gate blocks format changes. Hidden tar pairs block input-specific caching. Grader must build from /app source only, to block wrapping a system zstd (Debian zstd is not 1.5.7). Lock test edits and CMake flags in the grader's own build.
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden tar pairs for patch-from (wall-time median), hidden small-block sets, round-trip exactness, stock-decoder decodability, size <= baseline +1%. Executable oracle; hidden inputs differ from visible ones.
full_card.local_fit: C/cmake, 13 s build, 8 cores and 16 GB fit. Watch for 1.4 GB tar pairs at level 21 and noisy timing under gVisor.
full_card.lookup: partial. PR #4276 diff and description are public, naming the files and the CDict-skip idea. Approach is recallable in outline, not verbatim. No package-installable 1.5.7 offline.
full_card.provenance: facebook/zstd, v1.5.7 tag (BSD licence, repo pushed 2026-10-06, NOASSERTION spdx). Base is v1.5.6 as a history-less snapshot. Levers: PR #4276 (patch-from high levels), #4144/#4165 (small data), #4170 (dictionary), #4288 (ratio, changes bytes).
full_card.reference: zstd v1.5.7 upstream: patch-from lvl18 4.9x (210 s to 42.7 s on linux-6.13 vs 6.12, 6 threads); level-1 4 KB 280 to 310 MB/s. Public, BSD, C. Reward S=4.9 is our measurement, not the upstream one.
full_card.ships: Full zstd v1.5.6 C source snapshot, cmake, BSD licence. No git history past the base. Reference (1.5.7 source) is not shipped.
full_card.similarity: Neighbours: S-op-009 0.473 and S-op-006 0.448 (other seeds, likely overlapping zstd levers, check dedupe); zstd [ProgramBench] 0.197 (unverifiable, not found); zstd-decoder [SWE-Marathon] 0.188. Deliverable differs from both, so no K1 on this evidence.

Band.why: No dated public evidence of agents attempting this; the expected band is inferred from PR text, so it is capped at 3.

Build.why: Build is 13 s, but the grader needs a hand-built tar corpus and a test wiring that the probe did not produce; about 3-4 days.

Fit.why: C and cmake fit; 1.4 GB tar pairs and timing noise under gVisor are a risk.

Hor.why: The 8h tier is justified, but patch-from is largely one PR's worth of change; the rest is smaller levers.

Lic.why: BSD licence confirmed on LICENSE; the dual GPLv2 claim is not confirmed and spdx is NOASSERTION.

Multi.why: Three levers and several level and block-size buckets, but patch-from likely dominates the reward and the aggregation is unspecified.

Nov.why: zstd ProgramBench neighbour at 0.197 is above 0.15 and cannot be verified; deliverable differs from both public neighbours.

Real.why: Upstream zstd v1.5.7 release with public PRs (#4276, #4144 etc.) and measured numbers.

Ref.why: Complete BSD upstream reference with measured speedups; the 4.9x was measured on upstream's machine, not ours, so it is not fully calibrated.

Seal.why: Snapshot is history-less and the oracle is held out, but the public PR text and a famous codebase make recall of the approach plausible.

Surf.why: Executable oracle with hidden tar pairs and small-block sets, but the hidden set size is unconfirmed; not thousands of cases.

spike_plan.kill_if: Level-18 ratio is under 1.5x or the run-to-run spread exceeds 10%, or the 1.5.7 output fails the stock decoder.
spike_plan.pass_if: The v1.5.7 vs v1.5.6 time ratio at level 18 is at least 2x on the smaller pair (within the expected range of the 4.9x), sizes are within 1%, round-trips pass, and the ctest suite reports nonzero tests.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone facebook/zstd at tags v1.5.6 and v1.5.7 and build both with cmake Release (ZSTD_BUILD_TESTS=ON for the v1.5.6 check).

Build a patch-from pair from two versions of a mid-size tree (about 200-400 MB tar, e.g. two adjacent kernel or project releases). Time `zstd --patch-from=old -18 -T6` for v1.5.6 and v1.5.7 three times each.
Record ratio of times and compressed sizes; check the v1.5.7 output decodes with the v1.5.6 stock decoder and round-trips.
Repeat with level 1 on 4 KB blocks drawn from a Silesia-like set (benchmark mode) to check the 280 to 310 MB/s figure.
Run the v1.5.6 test suite via ctest with the tests built; confirm it reports nonzero tests, which closes the amber smoke result.
Check run-to-run spread; kill if it exceeds 10%.

v1.summary: The seed is real and public: zstd v1.5.7 is a BSD-licensed release with verified 4.9x patch-from and 280 to 310 MB/s small-block figures, and PR #4276 names the approach, so lookup is partial. It passes the gates with conditions: the grader needs a hand-built hidden corpus and working test wiring, and the reward's aggregation across levers must be spelled out so patch-from does not make it one-lever.

v2.note: Killed (K10). The facts are well confirmed (the 1.5.7 table, PR #4276, the BSD licence). But almost all of S comes from one small PR (#4276: skip the duplicate CDict and drop the wait on the first-job dictionary). An agent that profiles patch-from finds it quickly, and the PR's approach is public. The other levers (+10-20% small-block, ~5% dictionary) are within gVisor timing noise, so the reward collapses to one trick. zstd is on the CROWDED list, and sister seeds S-op-009/S-op-006 overlap (0.47/0.45). The reference diff is small, and measuring 200 s+ level-18 runs adds grading cost.
